# Migration - [`--add-reads`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/man/java.html#extra-options-for-java)

There can be a situation when a module needs to read something from another
module, but it does not define it in the `module-info.java` file. Consider the
following two JAR files as shown in the following table.

| JAR File     | JAR Type | Loaded As | Dependencies | Main Method |
| ------------ | -------- | --------- | ------------ | :---------: |
| `app.jar`    | Modular  | Named     | `domain.jar` |   **YES**   |
| `domain.jar` | Modular  | Named     |              |     No      |

The `app.jar` uses a package exported by the `domain.jar` but it does not
`requires` it in the `module-info.java` file (for demonstration purposes). We
can use the `--add-reads` command line option to allow the `app.jar` access the
`demo.domain` package, that is exported by the `domain.jar`.

> ```
> --add-reads module=target-module(,target-module)*
> ```
>
> Updates module to read the target-module, regardless of the module
> declaration. target-module can be all unnamed to read all unnamed modules.
([reference](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/man/java.html#extra-options-for-java))

This should be considered as a **temporary solution** until the module is
properly updated to require all the other modules.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created and copied to the
   `./target/libs` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR files

   ```
   ./target/libs
   ├── app.jar
   └── domain.jar

   1 directory, 2 files
   ```

2. List all modules

   ```shell
   java --module-path './target/libs' --list-modules
   ```

   All modules available on the module path

3. Describe the JAR files

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/domain.jar'
   ```

   The domain module description

   ```
   demo.domain@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/domain.jar!/module-info.class
   exports demo.domain
   requires java.base mandated
   ```

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/app.jar'
   ```

   The application module description

   ```
   demo.app@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/app.jar!/module-info.class
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo.app
   main-class demo.app.Main
   ```

4. Run the application

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   The application fails to launch because the application module does not
   require the domain module, so it is not loaded.

   ```
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: demo/domain/Quote
       at demo.app@1.0.0/demo.app.Main.main(Main.java:7)
   Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: demo.domain.Quote
       at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.loadClass(BuiltinClassLoader.java:580)
       at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:490)
       ... 1 more
   ```

   Read the `demo.domain` module from the `demo.app` module using the
   `--add-reads` command line option.

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --add-reads demo.app=demo.domain \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   Reading a module does not automatically load it. As the Java module system
   did not load the domain module, the application fails again.

   ```
   WARNING: Unknown module: demo.domain specified to --add-reads
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: demo/domain/Quote
       at demo.app@1.0.0/demo.app.Main.main(Main.java:7)
   Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: demo.domain.Quote
       at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.loadClass(BuiltinClassLoader.java:580)
       at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:490)
       ... 1 more
   ```

   Add the `demo.domain` module to the list of root modules using the
   `--add-modules` command line option.

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --add-modules demo.domain \
     --add-reads demo.app=demo.domain \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   This time the application works and prints the following.

   ```
   Learn from yesterday, live for today, hope for tomorrow. The important thing is not to stop questioning. by Albert Einstein
   ```

5. (*Optional*) For completeness, removing the `--add-reads` command line option
   will still not work. Both `--add-reads` and `--add-modules` are required.

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --add-modules demo.domain \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   This will fail to run because as the application module cannot access
   the exported packages from the domain module.

   ```
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalAccessError: class demo.app.Main (in module demo.app) cannot access class demo.domain.Quote (in module demo.domain) because module demo.app does not read module demo.domain
       at demo.app@1.0.0/demo.app.Main.main(Main.java:7)
   ```

   Exporting the package, by using the `--add-exports`, does not solve this
   problem either as this was already exported by the domain module.

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --add-modules demo.domain \
     --add-exports demo.domain/demo.domain=demo.app \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   This will fail to run because as the application module cannot access
   the exported packages from the domain module.

   ```
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalAccessError: class demo.app.Main (in module demo.app) cannot access class demo.domain.Quote (in module demo.domain) because module demo.app does not read module demo.domain
       at demo.app@1.0.0/demo.app.Main.main(Main.java:7)
   ```

6. (*Optional*) The `--add-reads` command line option can be used to allow a
   named module to read an unnamed module.

   In the following example, the `demo.domain` (`domain.jar`) module is loaded
   through the class path, which means it is an unnamed module.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/domain.jar' \
     --module-path './target/libs/app.jar' \
     --module 'demo.app'
   ```

   This will fail to run because as the application module cannot access
   the unnamed module.

   ```
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalAccessError: class demo.app.Main (in module demo.app) cannot access class demo.domain.Quote (in unnamed module @0x27716f4) because module demo.app does not read unnamed module @0x27716f4
       at demo.app@1.0.0/demo.app.Main.main(Main.java:7)
   ```

   This issue can be temporarily solved using the `--add-reads` command line
   option.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/domain.jar' \
     --module-path './target/libs/app.jar' \
     --add-reads demo.app=ALL-UNNAMED \
     --module 'demo.app'
   ```

   This time the application works and prints the following.

   ```
   Learn from yesterday, live for today, hope for tomorrow. The important thing is not to stop questioning. by Albert Einstein
   ```
